chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Mushriqi, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said:

I heard him say: 'Rather, His Hands are extended.' So I said to him: 'Two hands, like this?' And I pointed with my hand towards his hands. Then he said: 'No, if He were like this, He would have been a created thing.'

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ الرِّضَا: Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (Imam Musa al-Kadhim's son)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of Allah's Hands in Shia theology?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) refutes the literalist interpretation of divine hands by arguing that if they were physical limbs like humans, they would be created entities (makhluq), thereby preserving God's transcendence. This highlights the Shia theological stance against anthropomorphism (tashbih). The Imam's distinction underscores that divine attributes are real but not identical to created physical forms, a key concept in Usul al-Kalam.

en.basel-kadem: 16.	We were told by Muhammed bin Hasan bin Ahmad bin Waleed, may Allah be pleased with him, from Muhammed bin Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammed bin ‘Isa, from al-Mushriqi, from Abu’l-Hasan al-Rida, peace be upon him, that he said:

I heard him say: «Rather, His Hands are extended» [5:64] so I said: Does He have two hands, like this? And I pointed with my hand towards his hands. Then he said: No, if He was like this, He would have been (a) created (thing).
